b2-ecuador-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Volcano That Is Still Active
b2-ecuador-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are planning a trip to Ecuador and reading about its volcanoes. He asks which one is still active.
b2-ecuador-01.prompt: Tell Carlos which volcano is still active, with a relative clause.
cues: Say that it is still active
b2-ecuador-01.target: El Cotopaxi es un volcán que sigue activo.
b2-ecuador-01.english: Cotopaxi is a volcano that is still active.
b2-ecuador-01.canDo: I can describe a place or a person with a relative clause (*que*, *quien*).

b2-ecuador-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Islands Declared a Park
b2-ecuador-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are watching a documentary about the Galápagos, and she asks when the islands were protected.
b2-ecuador-02.prompt: Tell Meg when the islands were declared a national park, using the passive.
cues: Say what was done to the islands
b2-ecuador-02.target: Las islas fueron declaradas parque nacional en 1959.
b2-ecuador-02.english: The islands were declared a national park in 1959.
b2-ecuador-02.canDo: I can say what was done to a place with the passive (*fue declarada*, *fueron creadas*).

b2-ecuador-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Article Said
b2-ecuador-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you told him about your reading on Ecuador's indigenous movement the day before.
b2-ecuador-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that the day before you said you had read about the uprising, retelling with the right time word.
cues: Say that the day before you had read about the uprising
b2-ecuador-03.target: Dije que el día anterior había leído sobre el levantamiento.
b2-ecuador-03.english: I said that the day before I had read about the uprising.
b2-ecuador-03.canDo: I can retell what someone said, shifting the time and place words (*ese día*, *el día anterior*, *allí*).

b2-ecuador-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Fact That Nature Has Rights
b2-ecuador-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about Ecuador's 2008 constitution, and she asks what you think is important about it.
b2-ecuador-04.prompt: Tell Meg that the fact that nature has rights in the constitution is important.
b2-ecuador-04.target: El hecho de que la naturaleza tenga derechos en la Constitución es importante.
b2-ecuador-04.english: The fact that nature has rights in the constitution is important.
b2-ecuador-04.canDo: I can comment on a known fact with *el hecho de que* + subjunctive.

b2-ecuador-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Although the Vote Was Clear
b2-ecuador-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are preparing a short talk about Yasuní, and he asks what makes the topic difficult.
b2-ecuador-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that although the vote was clear, applying it is taking years.
cues: Say that applying it takes years
b2-ecuador-05.target: Si bien la consulta fue clara, su aplicación lleva años.
b2-ecuador-05.english: Although the vote was clear, applying it is taking years.
b2-ecuador-05.canDo: I can grant a point formally with *si bien* + indicative.

b2-ecuador-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Ecuador in Review
b2-ecuador-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk about Ecuador, and she asks which city has four rivers.
b2-ecuador-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg which city has four rivers, with a relative clause.
cues: Say that it has four rivers
b2-ecuador-consolidation.target: La ciudad que tiene cuatro ríos es Cuenca.
b2-ecuador-consolidation.english: The city that has four rivers is Cuenca.
b2-ecuador-consolidation.canDo: I can describe a place with a relative clause (*que*, *quien*).
